rule: Every new voxel-art project on World_server starts from this baseline, not from scratch - Godot OR browser/Three.js, this file name predates the browser port but the rules are engine-agnostic. These parameters were arrived at through real, verified iteration on dark-void-scene (including fixing the exact bugs listed below) and are now permanent defaults, not per-project choices. Only the user can relax or remove this rule.
engineAgnostic: 2026-08-29: user explicitly required the same rules to apply in the browser, not just Godot. shared/dark-void-scene-runtime.mjs (Three.js) is a verified port of the exact same formulas as the Godot version - same hash2/fbm1/ridgeHeight math, same ROCK_DARK/MID/LIT hex, same 5:1 voxel ratio, same true-orbit rig shape, same world/hero sibling separation. Use it as the browser reference implementation the same way orbit_camera_rig.gd/voxel_noise_utils.gd are the Godot reference.
provenIn: godot/dark-void-scene (World_server_navigator worktree, ai/opencode/navigator-engagement-v1) and apps/dark-void-scene (browser port, same worktree)

heroVoxelToWorldVoxelRatio.description: Hero/character voxels are always exactly 5x smaller than world/terrain voxels, both in individual cube size AND overall subject scale. Never build a hero at world voxel scale.

cameraPattern.description: Camera rig node is a child of the tracked subject, rig's OWN position is (0,0,0) at the subject's exact origin. The back/up offset lives only in the rig's internally-built camera child (set in _ready()), never duplicated as a second offset on the rig node's own scene-file transform. Movement lives on the tracked subject, driven by the rig's current facing.
cameraPattern.verification: game_eval-check the subject's global_position is identical before/after a real yaw change - only the camera should move

worldHeroSeparation.description: World/terrain objects and the hero are never parent/child. A 'hero embedded in the world' look at spawn is achieved by positioning the hero at the world object's socket coordinates, not by parenting.

materialPattern.description: StandardMaterial3D albedo_color=(1,1,1), vertex_color_use_as_albedo=true, roughness < 1.0 (never exactly 1.0 - it can't take a specular highlight, so no light can ever define its silhouette edges). Real per-instance colors from a dark/mid/lit palette lerp (extracted from an actual reference image when one exists), capped hard (~15-20% max toward the lit anchor, pow()-curved) so most of the silhouette stays dark - full-strength palette reads as a uniform warm wash.

lightingPattern.description: A DirectionalLight3D angled to graze across the hero/terrain silhouette, sky_mode=LIGHT_ONLY (value 1) so it doesn't paint an unwanted sun disc into a dark/void ProceduralSkyMaterial sky.

rendererForOldGpu.description: If the target machine has an old/weak GPU, Forward+ can silently crash on device selection with zero error output. Set renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility" (both desktop and .mobile) in project.godot and launch with --rendering-driver opengl3. Volumetric fog silently does not work under gl_compatibility (engine warning, not a crash) - use exponential/height fog properties instead for atmosphere on such targets.

verificationMethod.description: A type-inference-from-Variant issue (var x := expr where expr is a generic builtin like max()/min()/clamp() instead of the typed maxi/minf/clampf variants) is only a warning in the editor's live Play session, but can be a hard parse error in a real standalone run - the affected script fails to load with no player-visible error, often silently disabling the camera/controller. Always give such a var an explicit type, and always verify with a real standalone launch (godot.exe --path <project> --rendering-driver opengl3, NOT --editor), checking console output for SCRIPT ERROR / Parse Error lines - a screenshot from editor Play does not catch this.

mcpToolGotcha.description: godot-ai MCP's node_create tool's parent parameter is literally named parent_path, not parent. Passing parent is silently accepted and ignored (node lands at scene root). Always use parent_path.

browserOrbitRigPropertyNameGotcha.description: In the vendored three.js build used by this repo (shared/vendor/three), verified in isolation: an Object3D subclass instance with an own property literally named `pivot` (holding another Object3D) reproducibly corrupts that instance's own local matrix translation (NaN in elements[12..14]) during scene.updateMatrixWorld() - happens even with the child never added to the tree, and a different property name (same structure otherwise) does not reproduce it. Root cause unconfirmed (not present in the library's own source, so likely a harness/JIT-specific quirk), but trivial to avoid: never name such a property `pivot` on an Object3D subclass in this codebase - see shared/dark-void-scene-runtime.mjs's OrbitCameraRig, which uses `pitchGroup` instead.
